flare.note: the compact source.  The layer centre cx,cy is where the flare-anchored stack is positioned; it is NOT the reference's brightest point and the two should not be conflated, which an earlier version of this note did.  Measured on the reference: the compact peak sits 2.4-3.4 px EAST and 0.6-1.1 px NORTH of this cx,cy by the estimators that use R (the unclipped channel) or a sub-pixel translation fit, and 0.7-1.5 px east by the G and B centroids at low threshold -- those two are measuring the broad bloom, whose centroid agrees with this one to within 0.2-0.7 px.  The disagreement between the two is the finding: the PEAK is displaced and the BLOOM is not.  cx,cy is deliberately left where it is, because moving it drags all fifteen flare-anchored layers with it: measured at +3 px east that costs 0.0131 of whole-image MAE (1.8806 -> 1.8937) and 0.37 of flare r<110 (6.52 -> 6.90).  The displaced compact layer this note used to say was `not built` IS built now: flare_halo carries its own cx,cy at +3.00 east and -0.75 north, and its note has the measurements.  That the two must differ is itself measured and not an assumption: a ridge-masked sub-pixel translation fit of render against reference wants +3.00 east / -0.75 north at r < 10 and decays to +0.00 / -0.25 by r < 30, so the compact peak is displaced and the bloom around it is not

frame.corner_note: continuous-curvature corner: blend arc, main arc, blend arc; fits the measured corner outline to 0.13-0.27 px vs 0.66-0.84 px for a circular rounded rect. r_blend and corner_blend_deg are degenerate: what the corner fit measures is the lateral blend offset r_blend*(1-cos(blend_deg)) = 2.67 px, so r_blend is held at its fitted value and only the angle is searched
frame.note: SVG user units; centre-lines from opaque-bar fits to 371-461 cross-sections per edge
frame.radius_note: only used if corner_model is switched to 'squircle'; 171.8 is the best single circular radius

geometry.cubics_note: two cubic Beziers per curve joined at the apex with a vertical tangent; fitted to the sub-pixel ridge, RMS 0.085 px (left) / 0.095 px (right)
geometry.note: SVG user space = measured pixel-index + 0.5 (verified by rendering a line at a known coordinate and re-measuring it)

layers.note: the broad central wash. Its vertical extent is searched separately from its radius: the inter-curve region 90-150 px from either curve sits at 6.3 code values in the reference, so a round blob of this size over-fills the top and bottom of the lens

measured on a glow-free mask (20% of the interior): a single isotropic radial gradient centred well outside the canvas at (882,678.5) beats flat by 33% in G MAE; distance-to-frame explains only 4% of the variance (no vignette) and distance-to-the-arcs explains nothing, so the field is its own element
the reference's interior is brighter at the top than at the bottom by ~2.7 code values (row-band means), consistent with the rim being top-lit; this is that tilt

the light in the four interior corners. Measured in the lobes more than 40 px from a curve: within 100 px of the frame the corner quadrants read 9.5-11.0 code values in the reference against 7.0-8.3 rendered (30% too dark, 67k px), while the edge midpoints agree to 0.1-0.7. Nothing else in the model is corner-weighted on the inside

the interior corner light is not symmetric top to bottom: 12-45 px inside the frame the top corners read 13.7 code values against 8.3 at the bottom. One radial gradient cannot be both corner-weighted and top-weighted, so this second copy has its centre pushed *below* the icon, which makes the top corners the farthest and brightest points of its gradient

measured at |t|<62 with the flare excluded, the glow is 1.7x brighter on the concave side 11 px out and 5.9x brighter 100 px out, and the inter-curve midline 140 px from both curves sits at 3.9 code values against 13.5 in the lobes: the broad component lives inside the lens and is clipped to it

the only component offset towards the convex side. Every other glow stroke is inset into the lobe, which left the region 28-70 px between the curves 13-19% too dark while the lobe 14-38 px out was 6-11% too bright; one convex-biased stroke cuts the profile rms relative error from 8.6% to 7.0% at no cost to the global metric

D61: ACTED ON -- the paragraph below recorded a white excess this layer could not remove as one colour; it is now split: this layer keeps the cyan (white 0.377 -> 0.107, cyan 0.356 -> 0.378) and arc_glow1w carries the white on a taper along the curve.
MEASURED AND NOT ACTED ON -- the concave (lobe-facing) flank of both curves carries too much WHITE primary at essentially correct luminance, which is the measurable part of the standing 'pale' complaint at the curves.  In the 3-12 px band, excluding the flare (r > 200) and clipped pixels, dWhite = dR reads +5.38 on the left arc and +3.27 on the right, against -0.00 and -0.54 on the centre-facing side.  Reducing this layer's white from 0.37683 to 0.28 with cyan raised to 0.41 does improve both the target (lobe dR +4.33 -> +2.79) and the curve-band MAE (2.964 -> 2.938), and costs 0.0106 of whole-image MAE, which is a real regression elsewhere and an order of magnitude larger than the gains this iteration shipped.  The reason one symmetric layer cannot do it is in the numbers: the error is 5.38 against 3.27, a 1.6:1 left/right asymmetry, so any single value under-corrects one arc and over-corrects the other.  Honouring it needs this layer split per arc, which the `arc` primitive already supports.  Recorded here with the three tested values so the next pass starts from the measurement rather than from the complaint.
A NOTE ON HOW THIS WAS NEARLY DISMISSED: the first check of it used a cell that did not exclude the flare, where the render is too DARK in R, and read -4.09 -- the opposite sign.  The finding is real; the quick refutation was the thing that was wrong.

the WHITE half of arc_glow1, split out so white and cyan can vary along the curve independently (D61).  Same inset, width and blur as arc_glow1; its own ramp taper `glow1w` holds it at full strength on the flare's rows (y 495-535) and takes it to zero by y 290 and y 780.  Decomposing the outer-flank residual (d -12..-6 px) into white and cyan against A = [[1,0],[1,.94],[1,1]]: far from the flare the single-colour layer was too WHITE (white -8 to -10, cyan +7 to +19 cv), near it too CYAN (white +12 to +39) -- one colour cannot be both, which is the measurable part of the 'pale curves' complaint.  The split fixes the far excess and halves the near deficit; a narrow cyan deficit at d -8 (+7-8 G) remains and no inset or colour sweep of this pair moves it.

the 9-14 px band on the convex side ran 12-17% too dark with nothing narrow enough to fill it: arc_glow1 is inset into the lobe and reaches only 0.10 of its peak there, and arc_glow2b is four times too wide.  AND IT THEN BORROWED THE WRONG ALONG-CURVE PROFILE.  It was created to carry the convex side and given `arc_glow1`'s taper, which is the CONCAVE side's -- a curve that peaks where the arcs pass closest to the flare.  Measured in the taper's own coordinate, the convex band d 5-14 wanted the opposite: it was 7-10 cv too dark at y 160-280 and 720-840, at the arcs' ends, and 3-9 cv too BRIGHT at y 440-640 where the borrowed taper puts its maximum.  Solving for the coverage the band actually needs gives 70-100 units flat from y 200 to y 840, against the 27 -> 135 -> 17 the borrowed taper delivered: the convex side has essentially no along-curve taper over the arc body.  Hence its own `glow1b` ramp -- flat between y 220 and 830 with shoulders to zero at 87 and 945 -- and the amplitude down to 0.63 of what it was, since a flat profile at the old peak value would be far too much everywhere.  That is why raising this layer alone never worked: its taper concentrated it where it was already in excess, so the corridor gain was paid for in the flare.  Cross-curve error at d 5.5-13.5 goes from -11.3, -9.5, -7.6, -6.1, -5.1, -4.2, -3.5, -2.2, -1.0 cv to -2.7, -1.0, +0.2, +0.5, +0.1, -0.6, -1.2, -0.8, -0.4.  Its inset, width and blur were re-searched after the taper changed and all three were already at the optimum.

D62: both curves are WHITER on their concave side at the flare's height than the glow terms draw -- R 20-59 cv short at 3-18 px from the ridge within |dy| ~40 of the core row, on the left curve 66 px from the core as much as on the right one, so it is the curves' light and not the flare's.  A white glow 16 px out, 8 wide, blur 4, flat over |dy| 15 and gone by |dy| 55 (fitted over both concave sides, |dy| <= 90: rms 10.19 -> 8.28; no cyan wanted).

the isolated flare is below 0.01 in additive luminance beyond r ~ 130 px and indistinguishable from zero beyond ~160, so this widest bloom ends there; the broad light between the curves is the central field, not the flare.
MEASURED, NOT ACTED ON -- the flare's mid-radius colour error.  In the annulus r 20-55 the render carries too much of the WHITE primary and too little cyan at nearly constant luminance, which is what makes the surround read as a white wash instead of a cyan bloom and is the measurable part of the standing under-saturation complaint.  Per-channel mean(render - reference), ridge clearance 8, unclipped, at r 20-40 / 40-55:
    north  dR +12.3/+3.8   dG -4.8/-6.5   dB -6.4/-10.2
    south  dR  +4.1/+5.1   dG +0.7/-5.5   dB +3.6/-6.9
    nw     dR  -1.0/+6.4   dG -6.1/-2.3   dB -7.5/-5.6
    sw     dR  -7.6/+7.9   dG -4.2/-9.4   dB -1.4/-8.4
against a 36-placement matched null at z = +27 for the north cell, where the luminance difference is only +0.4 and sees almost none of it.
THE MODEL CANNOT CORRECT IT WITH THE LEVERS IT HAS, and three separate attempts establish that rather than assert it.  (1) Both halo layers are already at maximum amplitude -- white 1.0 and cyan 1.0 -- so the only levers are geometric.  A 9-point sweep of the pair's e-folding (halo 0.14/0.17/0.20 x this layer 0.246/0.32/0.40) leaves the shipped 0.20/0.2464 the MAE optimum: the best chroma cell, 0.14/0.32, improves the colour statistic from 5.73 to 4.99 and costs MAE 1.8886 -> 1.9414.  (2) Adding a NEW mid-radius cyan halo (four geometries, r 48-75) gets the chroma statistic to 5.14 for 0.0035 of MAE and 0.10 of flare-region MAE -- a tenth of the defect for a measurable regression.  (3) The reason both fail is that the error is ANISOTROPIC and every lever here is isotropic: the same annulus that is too white to the north and south is too DIM in red due west (dR -6.9 at r 20-40), so an elliptical halo cannot move white out of one and into the other.  Correcting it needs an angular colour decomposition -- white moved from the isotropic halo into a horizontal carrier, with the cyan raised to hold the luminance -- fitted against per-direction per-radius colour cells.  That is a rebuild of the bloom's colour basis and it is deliberately not attempted as a parameter change  D62: the exp(-u/0.2464) law is now a TABLE -- verbatim beyond u 0.28 (r ~39), its six inner stops refitted to the reference's unclipped G and B at r 10-44 outside the curves: the law put G +6..+11 and B +5..+9 too much cyan at r 10-26 in EVERY direction, the near-core ring the eye reads as too cyan; after the refit +1..+2 / ~0.  u=0 (r<8, clipped white in both images) is not measurable and is the monotone extrapolation of the next two stops.  A table has no single knob, so its search bound was removed.

D61: squash 0.6453 -> 0.514.  The core's white is now shared with flare_core_w (compact) and flare_cloud_w (west), so this layer no longer has to supply the north/south white the reference lacks: R residual north/south -12.1 -> -3.8 cv.  The reasoning below about squash was about the halo ALONE and stands for that.
u = 2.757*exp(-sqrt((dx/22.7)^2+(dy/16.9)^2)) fitted over 63k px of the isolated flare.  squash was lowered to 0.62 during iteration 6 and is back at 0.6453.  The reason given for lowering it does NOT stand: `the core is too tall`, measured as an R half-width excess of 1.1-2.9 px north and south from each image's own peak against a westward match, was an alignment artefact.  Displacing the shipped render against ITSELF by (3.02 east, 0.70 north) -- the registration error corrected by this layer's cx,cy below -- reproduces 71% of the claimed aspect contrast with zero model error, and once the two are registered the remaining anisotropy is +1.4 to +1.9 cv at z 1.3-1.8.  An aspect measured from each image's own peak is not an aspect measurement when the peaks are 3 px apart.  Re-measured on the CORRECTED model -- spike profile fixed, this layer re-centred -- with nothing varying but squash, 0.58 / 0.62 / 0.6453 give whole-image MAE 1.87888 / 1.87817 / 1.87815, flare r<110 6.4775 / 6.4578 / 6.4574, r<40 MAE 9.847 / 9.656 / 9.610, west angular residual RMS over 55 ridge-masked bins at r 34/40/46 7.110 / 6.235 / 5.734 cv, the ridge-masked north and south r 20-40 red deficit -7.36/-10.68, -5.56/-8.87, -4.46/-7.78 cv, visual_regression's white-radius ratio 0.872 / 0.872 / 0.897 (1.0 = the reference), against the ridge-masked r 6-20 luminance excess +3.53 / +4.37 / +4.88 cv and a core-box MAE (x 516-548, y 500-530) of 5.963 / 6.121 / 6.328.  Six statistics prefer 0.6453 and two prefer 0.58; 0.62 is best at none of them.  It is reverted, not re-optimised: the pre-iteration value is restored because the argument that moved it was wrong, and the two statistics that still want a smaller squash -- both core brightness rather than core shape -- are the isotropic r 6-20 over-brightness, whose lever is amplitude and not aspect.  That lever was swept: scaling this layer's white to 0.92 and 0.85 halves the r 6-20 excess and costs whole-image MAE (+0.0009, +0.0026), the west angular RMS (4.11 -> 4.51 -> 5.00 in that sweep's own units) and the core r<30 MAE (9.277 -> 9.356 -> 9.723) together, so it is left at 1.0.  What no value of squash fixes is the r 20-40 excess, which is a colour error and not a shape one -- see the note on flare_halo_far.  cx,cy sit +3.00 px east and -0.75 px north of flare.cx,cy, and are the model's answer to the displaced compact peak that flare's own note describes.  Measured about the SAME fixed x and y in both images -- no per-image peak, so no registration to get wrong -- the reference's east-west asymmetry over |dx| 2-7, rows +-5, in R is +14.50 cv and the unshifted render's is -16.13; north-south -2.56 against +6.73.  Moving the whole anchor instead (flare.cx += 3) is the wrong vehicle and was measured: it drags the streaks, the vertical line and the rays off structures they are registered to and costs 0.0131 of whole-image MAE and 0.37 of flare r<110, while moving the high-pass centroid only 0.5 px for a 3 px anchor move.  A ridge-masked sub-pixel translation fit of render against reference says why: it wants +3.00 east / -0.75 north at r < 10 in R, +2.00 / -0.50 at r < 20, and +0.00 / -0.25 by r < 30, so the compact peak is displaced and the bloom around it is not.  Moving this one layer degrades nothing, all measured at the shipped squash with nothing else varying -- whole MAE 1.87836 -> 1.87815, flare r<110 6.4632 -> 6.4574, core-box MAE (x 516-548, y 500-530) 8.087 -> 6.328, r<40 9.856 -> 9.610, the ridge-masked r 6-20 luminance excess +8.28 -> +4.88 cv, E-W -16.13 -> +6.68, N-S +6.73 -> -3.10.  That r 6-20 row is the one to note: more than half of the `isotropic core over-brightness` that survived the aspect refutation was itself the registration error.  +3.00 is the largest correction that degrades nothing, NOT the best fit.  MAE and the flare annulus are slightly better at +1.50 and +2.25 (1.87796, 6.4520/6.4522) and the asymmetry alone wants about +4.2 px; +3.75 and +4.50 keep improving the core box (6.087, 6.006) and the E-W match (+12.06, +16.61) while whole MAE turns (1.87849, 1.87906), the first value worse than no shift at all.  What none of them fixes is the trench at x 538-541, where the render is still 29-40 cv dark over y 500-540: the reference's core reaches the right arc and this centro-symmetric layer cannot reach it without overshooting the west.

the compact white core (D61): a small white radial on the halo's centre, so the core's white is a compact term plus the broad halo instead of one exposure setting.  Its amplitude is set by the core's own R ring means, not by a global fit: swept 0.50 / 0.42 / 0.35 / 0.28 / 0.20, the R mean at r 0-4 runs 237.7 / 236.6 / 235.8 / 234.8 / 233.6 against the reference's 233.0, the R>=200 extent along the core row and column goes W9 E17 N5 S6 -> W8 E17 N5 S5 (reference W8 E17 N4 S5), and whole-image, flare r<110 and core r<25 MAE all improve monotonically down to 0.20 -- the earlier 0.5 made the core both larger and whiter than the reference's.

the lumpy white cloud west of the core (D61).  R residual west of the core was +15.8 cv (reference whiter) against -12.1 north/south before it; a single squashed halo cannot put white west without putting it north and south too.  Radial, centred 25 px west of the core.  The reference's cloud is lumpy and this is smooth, which is recorded as a remaining difference rather than modelled with invented lumps.

the cyan glow that fills the lens interior around the flare (D61).  With the triangular wedges gone and the lower-left rays drawn at their measured strength, the lens interior near the flare read 12-14 cv too DARK in G at r 20-40 over theta 210-270 and 8-10 cv at r 40-60 -- light the wedges and the over-bright rays had been supplying in the wrong SHAPE.  This supplies it as a soft ellipse (exp falloff, no straight edge anywhere), fitted on the Gaussian-smoothed (sigma 5) residual inside the lens.  Removing it costs 0.012 whole-image MAE and 0.33 flare r<110 MAE.

D61: both side profiles are now measured TABLES fitted to the reference's along-row amplitude (rows 511-513 minus rows 506/507/516/517 per 15 px bin, R, G, B).  The east side was twice too bright past dx 90 (G 10.9 / 9.7 / 8.6 at dx 93-123 against 7.8 / 5.5 / 3.3) and the west exp law was too flat near and too steep far; both now track the reference within ~1.5 cv along the whole row.  The near-core WHITE the reference shows on this row is flare_streak_w's.
line A, on the core.  Its rendered row is calibrated against the isolated basis (row = cy - 0.547), not against FLARE_CORE's y, which is the centroid of a saturated core and reads 1.1 px low

the white part of line A (D61).  Along the streak row the reference is WHITER than the model BESIDE the core and cyan far from it: R above the local trend reads 35.9 / 47.0 / 39.6 cv at dx -57 / -42 / -27 against 16.7 / 24.4 / 25.0 in the model, while G already matched.  One streak has one colour, so the white is its own thin streak on the same row.  Its profile is a measured TABLE that is ZERO at the core and peaks 20-50 px out: an exp law peaking at the core put the white where the core is already white enough and pushed the R>=200 extent west from 8 to 11 px.  Now R reads 32.0 / 46.1 / 40.9 at the same three places and the core extent is back to the reference's.

D61: no longer clamped white.  white 1.008 -> 0.605 with cyan/blue kept in proportion renders (154, 224, 255) instead of (255, 255, 255), and sigma_y 0.4 -> 0.9: at dx 30-110 east the reference's line is 2.5 rows FWHM with near-equal R/G/B increments (18.0 / 17.5 / 19.5 cv) and the model's was a 2-row, R-heavy stroke (18.4 / 11.7 / 11.2).  The tables' tails were refitted: beyond the left curve the reference has no line (G -1.5 to 2.6 at x 380-460) where the model drew one.
line B, the narrowest and whitest of the three and 3.5x too dim before this.  Its sigma_y bound of 1.3 made the measured 2.1-2.7 px FWHM unreachable, which is why fitting it only turned it down.  Its longitudinal profile is now a MEASURED pair of tables, west in `profile` and east in `profile_e`, not the exp(-t/0.216) law it had.  The law put screen-domain A*k = 0.39 on the line at the core, where the reference puts 0.00-0.06: over rows 519-520, x 517-538, the reference's R declines monotonically 187.3 / 182.5 / 171.0 / 162.2 at y 518/519/520/521 with no bump at all, while the render rose to 213.2 and 208.6 -- a 31-38 cv bar across the core that the exp law could not avoid because it peaks at the origin.  At |dx| 30-80 the same line matched to 1-5 cv, so the amplitude was right and the shape was wrong.  Measured as the screen-domain bump above the linear trend through y 517 and y 522, the reference's A*k runs, west, 0.055 / 0.168 / 0.184 / 0.104 / 0.050 / 0.019 / 0.015 / 0.014 / 0.007 and, east, 0.020 / 0.000 / 0.092 / 0.115 / 0.113 / 0.067 / 0.032 / 0.019 / 0.002 at |dx| 3-12 / 12-20 / 20-28 / 28-38 / 38-50 / 50-65 / 65-85 / 85-110 / 110-140: non-monotone on both sides, peaking near |dx| 24 west and 35 east.  A*k is 0.48 x profile over t <= 0.5 in this stack, so the tables are those numbers divided by 0.48.  Honest limits: inside |dx| 20 east the reference sits at 230 cv, where the estimator resolves only about 0.04 in A*k, so the 0.000 reading there means `small`, not `zero`, and the west values at |dx| 50-85 sit on the left arc ridge and are worth +-0.01.  Deleting the line outright is worse than either (row-band MAE 10.03 against 7.78 measured, 7.84 for the exp law).

line C: dy +19.33, rises from an inner cut-off near |dx| 80, peaks at 110-170, then falls -- an explicit table because no monotone law fits  D62: line C's EAST side has its own table, the west one compressed by 0.9, and east_gain 0.85 -> 1.10: tools/line_report.py's line C at dx +95..+240 read 3.13/3.92/3.51/1.98/0.87 against the reference's 4.61/4.78/3.91/0.97/0.45.  The west was re-scored and left: no stretch or gain improved it.

the horizontal wash's NEAR, WHITE half.  It was half_len 123.2 and is 62 with its profile scale rescaled by 123.2/62 so the falloff IN PIXELS is unchanged -- the scale is in units of half_len, so shortening without rescaling would have changed the shape as well as the extent.  Truncation alone improves MAE; the far field it used to cover is now flare_wash_far's, and is cyan rather than white.
This layer is still the only red source in the near field and must not be recoloured: recolouring it cyan at equal G opens a 15-33 cv red hole over r 12-32 (dR -22.2/-29.2/-20.7 at r 12-18/18-25/25-32) while improving r 32-78 by 4-9 cv.  A control that only ADDS a pure-cyan far wash leaves dR bit-identical at every radius, which is the direct proof that white is the only red carrier here.
Its amplitude is 0.48 and not the 0.60 a global photometric refit chose.  The refit was run over the whole stack and then only four layers were transplanted, so its near-field budget did not survive the transplant: at 0.60 the azimuthal red residual at r 12-18 is +16.9 cv and the north/south R excess at r 8-20 is +17.1/+14.0, against +7.5 and +6.7/+2.2 at 0.48.  What does NOT change across that span is whole-image MAE (1.8861 to 1.8872) or the sum of the absolute azimuthal red residuals over r 12-55 (31.2 to 33.1 at every setting tried), because lowering this layer trades the r 12-18 excess against the r 18-32 deficit one for one.  That is the mis-distribution below, restated as a fact about the search: no scalar amplitude can fix a shape error.
KNOWN AND NOT FIXED: its red is mis-distributed in radius even now -- too much inside r 18, 4-8 cv too little at 18-32, too much again at 32-78 -- because it is a monotone exponential from r 0 where the reference wants an annulus.  The earlier record that the near field was 'correct to +0.50 cv at r 12-25' is an average of +11.05 at r 12-18 and -3.81 at 18-25, two opposite errors, which is not the same thing

the horizontal line's BROAD component, and the missing half of it.  A transverse cut through the reference's line is two things at every distance: a narrow spike, and a wash of sigma 12-18 px that carries 70-94% of the light.  The reconstruction reproduced the wash inside |dx| ~80 and had essentially NONE beyond, which is the whole of 'too thin, too hard, isolated' -- not the core's width, which matches (reference sigma 1.3-2.8 px against the render's 1.45-1.8).  North-flank skirt fraction, three baseline annuli, reference against the old render: 0.71/0.71/0.70 vs 0.30/0.48/0.54 at |dx| 80-130, and 0.69/0.72/0.70 vs -0.38/-0.25/0.32 at 130-190, where the render's statistic is unstable precisely because its numerator is zero.  Against a matched null at the same cell displaced 110/150/190 rows: 11, 7.4 and 2.5 sigma.
IT IS PURE CYAN because it is the BROAD component whose colour changes with distance, not the spike.  Broad-component R/G: 0.97 +- 0.09 at |dx| 18-45, then -0.03 +- 0.05 at 80-130 and -0.07 to +0.10 beyond.  The narrow spike shows no distance trend at all (0.15-0.35 everywhere) and is left alone.  The white-to-cyan transition is bracketed at |dx| 45-70 and NOT localised more finely: it rests on one 14-column east band, and whether it is a step or a ramp is unresolved.
The profile is tabulated because it rises to a peak near |dx| 70 and then falls slowly; no monotone law does that.  Amplitudes for this layer, flare_fan and flare_streak were fitted together -- the narrow line had been standing in for the missing wash and had to come down 28% in white when the wash arrived  sigma_y was 14.0 and is 10.0, and the lower bound was 8.0, so a search could not have reached the minimum at all: the same mistake as flare_spike's sigma_y bound of 1.3, and the reason the bound is now 4.0.  14 came from a transverse-sigma estimate quoted as `10-18 px depending on how the floor is set`, i.e. from a range, not a fit.  Fitted against the reference over this layer's own footprint (|dy| <= 30, 60 <= |dx| <= 300, both sides, arc ridges masked at 22 px), sigma_y 8 / 9 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 14 gives footprint MAE 1.848 / 1.853 / 1.864 / 1.880 / 1.903 / 1.944, whole-image MAE 1.87779 / 1.87792 / 1.87817 / 1.87859 / 1.87920 / 1.88051 (measured before flare_halo's squash was reverted, which shifts all six by about +0.00002 and reorders none), and a skirt ratio (visual_regression's own statistic, 1.0 = the reference) of 0.877 / 0.930 / 0.974 / 1.008 / 1.035 / 1.087.  10 is not a compromise between the two instruments: it beats 14 on all three, including the skirt, which at 14 was overshooting by 8.7% rather than short.  Amplitude is unchanged; scaling it 0.6-0.9 trades the two sides against each other without improving either.  The width cannot be right everywhere, and this is why: at |dx| 135-185 east the reference's transverse tail above the |dy| 34-46 floor reads 4.09 / 1.99 / 1.57 / 0.61 cv at dy -8 / -16 / -22 / -28, which a sigma-14 Gaussian through the -8 point predicts as 2.51 / 1.40 / 0.65 and a sigma-8 one as 0.91 / 0.15 / 0.00 -- the far band wants 14 -- while at |dx| 60-110 east the sigma-14 render was +2.6 to +3.5 cv too bright at every dy from -12 to -28.  A streak carries one sigma_y along its whole length. In the two unclipped channels the reference's line RISES across that boundary and peaks at |dy| 36-70 -- where this table puts its collapse -- and the model's non-monotone tail bump at |dy| 80-100 is absent from the reference altogether. What was originally offered as the reason for tabulating rather than fitting a law.  Three things are deliberately absent: no broad halo (the flank at |dx| 3-8 is consistent with zero), nothing past |dy| 110 (pooled 110-240 is within 1.3 cv of zero at 95%), and nothing east of the core, where the right ridge allows only an 11.6 cv limit and the honest position is silence. south_gain was 1.0 -- a DEFAULT, never a measurement, and one that could not have been searched either: `sigma_x` and `south_gain` both carried bounds here and neither name was in the optimiser's key list, so they were frozen through every run that reported optimising shapes.  The reference's line is north-dominated.  south/north of A_4 over |dy| 36-110: reference 0.44 in B and 0.63 in R, against the shipped render's 0.97 and 1.19; at 0.55 the render reads 0.45 and 0.65.  B is the channel to trust for this -- it runs 50-119 cv in these bands with nothing clipped at either end, while R is FLOOR-clipped there (20.5%, 30.5% and 19.7% exact zeros at |dy| 26-36, 36-50 and 50-70).  A block bootstrap over 8-row blocks gives B 0.52 [0.28, 0.84] with P(south >= north) = 0.004; the honest range is 0.45-0.85 and the estimators disagree systematically inside it (a narrow centre-minus-flank statistic says 0.35-0.42, A_4 says 0.52-0.63, a 4x downsample says 0.75), so 0.55 is a choice within a range and not a measurement to two figures.  The pooled statistic in tools/vstreak_report.py was blind to all of this and actively penalised the fix, which is why that tool now reports the two sides separately.  sigma_x 1.7 was re-measured at the same time and SURVIVES: the width-sensitive ratio N/A_4 puts it at 1.44-1.60 in G and B and 0.95-1.35 in the floor-clipped R, so 1.5 is marginally better supported but the difference is below the render's own resolution.  The amplitude inside |dy| 16 is unconstrained -- the bloom's own curvature dominates there -- so the inner stop is continuity, not a measurement  THE SOUTH IS NOT A CONSTANT FRACTION OF THE NORTH, which is all a single south_gain can say. tapers.note: core/glow1..3 are the measured station-by-station fades of the core coverage and of the three glow gaussians' G amplitudes (out/analysis/arc_photometry.json). core_wide is the extra width the core gains towards mid-height. | haze and glow2b are ramps, not measured tables: both layers postdate the station-by-station cross-section fit, so reusing glow3's table for them would be an assumption dressed as a measurement. Resolving the profile error by |t| band showed exactly why it matters: at |t| 40-62 deg the concave side was +13 to +27% too bright and the convex side 9-15% too dark, i.e. the glow is less one-sided towards the tips than glow3's fade allows.
